title: The "press Play to update" banner shows on every page, with no Play button
summary: Every page shows a banner saying "A YG Dolphin update is out: press Play to update." It appears to signed-out visitors and on pages that have nothing to do with the desktop app (Sign in, What you can upload, Support, SDK, browser games like GlobeTap). There is no Play button on most of those pages, so the instruction can't be followed, and new visitors don't know what YG Dolphin is.
steps: Open https://yougame.co/specs (or /support, /upload, /g/globetap) while signed out.
Look at the very top of the page.
expected: The update notice only shows to people who have the desktop app (or who play a game that needs it), ideally on the game page next to the Play button, and it can be dismissed.
actual: The banner shows on every page, to everyone, and the page it appears on usually has no Play button.

notes: Banner text, verbatim: "A YG Dolphin update is out: press Play to update."
Seen on: /, /?sort=top, /?sort=new, /upload, /specs, /sdk, /support, /source, /how-it-works, /feature-requests, /g/globetap, /g/perfect-circle-live-competitive-multiplayer.

Browser check (Playwright Chromium 1280x800, signed out, 2026-10-18): Banner "A YG Dolphin update is out: press Play to update." shows at the top of /specs for a signed-out visitor; no Play button on the page. Also seen on every other page visited this run.

agent_prompt:
On yougame.co, the site-wide banner "A YG Dolphin update is out: press Play to update." renders on every page for every visitor, including signed-out users and pages without a Play button (/specs, /support, /upload, /g/globetap).

Fix:
1. Find the component that renders this banner (search the codebase for "press Play to update").
2. Only render it when (a) the visitor has the desktop app / Orca installed and its version is older than the latest, or (b) the current page is a game page whose game runs in Orca (e.g. /g/open-brawl, /g/project-rollback).
3. On game pages, place the notice next to the Play button so "press Play" refers to something visible.
4. Add a dismiss (x) button and remember dismissal per version (localStorage key including the version), so it reappears only for the next update.
5. Use one product name in the copy (see BUG-07) and link the name to /help/orca.

Acceptance: signed-out visitor on /specs sees no banner; a game page for an Orca game shows the notice beside Play; dismissing hides it until the next version.

title: Game pages ask for leaderboard scores even when the leaderboard is off, logging a console error
summary: Every game page asks the server for the visitor's best score, even for games with the leaderboard turned off. The server answers 403 "The leaderboard is off for this game.", and the browser logs it as an error. Players don't see anything break, but it's a wasted request on each page view and it buries real errors in the console and in error monitoring.
steps: Open https://yougame.co/g/globetap (also /g/open-brawl, /g/project-rollback) with DevTools open.
Look at the Console and Network tabs.
expected: No scores request when the game's leaderboard is off, or a 200 response with an empty result.
actual: GET /api/scores?slug=globetap&period=all&limit=1&player=<guest id> returns 403 {"error":"The leaderboard is off for this game.","code":"board_off"} and the console shows "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 403 (Forbidden)".

notes: Seen on /g/globetap, /g/open-brawl and /g/project-rollback in the browser check (Playwright Chromium 1280x800, signed out, 2026-10-18).
Response body: {"error":"The leaderboard is off for this game.","code":"board_off"}
Screenshot shows the GlobeTap page; the evidence is in the console and network log below.
console: error: Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 403 (Forbidden)

agent_prompt:
On yougame.co game pages (/g/<slug>), the client calls GET /api/scores?slug=<slug>&period=all&limit=1&player=<guest id> for every game. For games whose leaderboard is disabled, the API returns 403 {"error":"The leaderboard is off for this game.","code":"board_off"}, which logs a console error on every page view (seen on /g/globetap, /g/open-brawl, /g/project-rollback).

Fix (do both):
1. Client: find where the game page fetches the player's best score (search for "/api/scores" and "limit=1"). Only make the request when the game's data says the leaderboard is enabled (the page already knows, since it decides whether to render the leaderboard panel).
2. API: in the /api/scores handler, return 200 with {"enabled":false,"scores":[]} for board_off instead of 403. Keep 403 for real permission failures.
3. Make sure the client treats enabled:false as "no leaderboard" without logging.

Acceptance: loading /g/globetap signed out produces no /api/scores request (or a 200), and the console shows no 403.

title: A ranked player is named "REMOTE CODE EXECUTION" on the Project+ leaderboard
summary: The Project+ ranked leaderboard shows a player called "REMOTE CODE EXECUTION" at #6. It isn't a slur, but on a page where players install a desktop emulator and commenters already ask whether it is safe, a name like that reads as a security warning and can scare people off. Gamer tags appear to go live with no name filter or review.
steps: Open https://yougame.co/g/project-rollback.
Scroll to Top players (Ranked).
expected: Gamer tags that imitate system or security messages (and slurs) are blocked when someone sets them, and existing ones can be reset by a moderator.
actual: #6 on the ranked leaderboard: "REMOTE CODE EXECUTION", 1231 ELO.

notes: Leaderboard read on 2026-10-18: #1 The Doctor 1334, ... #6 REMOTE CODE EXECUTION 1231, ... #10 xX_CerealKiD69_Xx 1223.
The page comments include a question about RCE safety, which makes the name more alarming.
Browser check (2026-10-18): Top players panel, 402 ranked players, shows #6 REMOTE CODE EXECUTION, 37W 4L, Gold II, 1231 ELO.

agent_prompt:
On yougame.co, gamer tags are shown on public leaderboards and comments with no apparent name filtering. Example: the Project+ ranked leaderboard (/g/project-rollback) shows a player named "REMOTE CODE EXECUTION" at #6, which reads as a security warning on a page that asks players to install a desktop emulator.

Fix:
1. Find where gamer tags are created and changed (sign-up form "Gamer tag" field and the account settings endpoint).
2. Add server-side validation: reject tags matching a blocklist of slurs and of system/security-scare phrases (e.g. "remote code execution", "rce", "virus", "hacked", "admin", "moderator", "yougame", "support", "official"), normalising case, spacing, leetspeak and repeated characters first. Return a clear error ("Pick a different tag").
3. Give admins a way to reset a tag to a neutral default ("Player1234") and to flag a tag from the leaderboard or a comment via the existing Report flow.
4. Run the new validator over existing tags and list matches for manual review; don't auto-rename.

Acceptance: setting the tag "Remote Code Execution" fails with a helpful message; an admin can reset an existing offending tag.

title: Leaving a Word Duel lobby leaves stale room controls in the page sidebar
summary: After a signed-out player leaves a Word Duel friend lobby and returns to the game page, the sidebar still looks attached to the departed room. The Seats list is empty, Add local player remains enabled but does nothing, and room chat still targets the old room. Reloading restores the initial sidebar. This is a confusing dead-end in the page UI; the reproduction does not establish that multiplayer itself is broken.
steps: In a fresh signed-out Chrome tab, open https://yougame.co/g/word-duel and press Play.
Inside the game, choose 1v1 Duel, then Play with a friend.
Confirm that the platform lobby opens with 1/2 seats and you as host.
Choose Leave lobby, then Back to the page.
Inspect the page sidebar, try Add local player, and inspect the Sign in link target in the CHAT panel.
Reload the page and compare the sidebar with the state immediately after leaving.
expected: Leaving the lobby clears the page sidebar’s active room state. Returning to the page shows the initial “Invite friends and you all land in the same room” state, hides controls for the departed room, and removes its room-specific chat and sign-in target.
actual: The Seats list is empty, but the sidebar still says “Choose players and start inside the game.” Add local player stays enabled and has no effect. The CHAT panel and its Sign in next URL still refer to the departed room. Reloading resets the sidebar correctly.

notes: Verified by the cloud gameplay tester in two independent fresh signed-out Chrome tabs on Linux, approximately 1180×750, during the 2026-10-19 03:36–03:51 UTC playtest. Reproduction rooms: 9gfr833c and 8gmdzema.

The screenshot captures the reproduced post-leave state: Word Duel is back on its mode screen, while the page sidebar still shows Lobby, “Choose players and start inside the game”, Add local player, and room chat.

The empty Seats list, ineffective Add local player action, stale Sign in next URL, and reload recovery were checked during the interactive reproductions. The static screenshot alone does not demonstrate those interactions or the URL target.
Severity low / P3: stale room UI creates a confusing dead end after leaving. No claim that multiplayer itself is broken.

agent_prompt:
On https://yougame.co/g/word-duel, reproduce in a fresh signed-out session: Play → 1v1 Duel → Play with a friend → confirm the platform lobby has 1/2 seats with you as host → Leave lobby → Back to the page. The page sidebar retains “Choose players and start inside the game”, an enabled Add local player button that does nothing, and room chat whose Sign in next URL still targets the departed room. Its Seats list is empty. Reloading restores the initial sidebar.

Find how the leave-lobby flow updates the page’s active room state and ensure returning to the page clears all state derived from the departed room. Restore the initial “Invite friends and you all land in the same room” sidebar, hide departed-room controls and chat, and remove the stale room target from the sign-in return URL. Avoid assuming the underlying multiplayer session or transport is broken.

Acceptance: complete the sequence twice without reloading; each time the sidebar returns to its initial state and no control or link targets the departed room. Creating or joining a subsequent lobby shows only that current room’s state.

notes: Verified by the cloud gameplay tester in signed-out Chrome on Linux, approximately 1180×750, during the 2026-10-19 03:36–03:51 UTC playtest. Primary reproduction: search Word Duel → Multiplayer → Newest → submit the same search again.

Before screenshot: Word Duel query, selected Multiplayer and Newest controls, and result text “1 game matches ‘Word Duel’ (multiplayer)”. After screenshot: the same query, neither player mode selected, For you selected, and the multiplayer qualifier removed from the result text.

On yougame.co, search Word Duel, select Multiplayer and Newest, and confirm the URL is /?q=Word+Duel&players=multi&sort=new. Click Search again without changing the query. The URL becomes /?q=Word+Duel, Multiplayer and Newest clear, and For you is restored. A separate reproduction starting with RPG + Single player + Newest retains genre=RPG when searching Word Duel, but drops players and sort.

Find the search submission logic and preserve the current player filter, sort, and genre when updating the query. Keep the URL, selected controls, and displayed results consistent. Change these settings only through their explicit controls or a clearly requested reset.

Acceptance: resubmitting an identical query preserves players=multi and sort=new and keeps Multiplayer and Newest selected. Searching Word Duel from RPG + Single player + Newest preserves all three selections. Verify both the URL parameters and the visible selected state. This fix concerns search-state persistence; it does not require redesigning the filter row.
